propositions: The live tickets branch .bridge_state/projects.json was overwritten with rehearsal fixture keys LEG/ONE/TWO/ZERO that do not exist in live REB Jira Cloud, causing the Reconcile Bridge scheduled action to fail with JQL parse error on every run since 2026-08-15T02:39Z.

The fetcher._build_snapshot multi-project fan-out iterates over every key in projects.json and issues jql_active(proj) queries; when projects.json contains nonexistent keys, the first query fails at Jira validation even though the key passes local _PROJECT_KEY_RE regex, aborting reconcile_once and exiting with code 1.

The corruption arrived via ad-hoc git commits (9f1b2cff98, 275bd7507e) on the live tickets branch authored by the test-fixture identity at 2026-08-15T02:18Z, 21 minutes before the first consistent failure, violating the unified store write lock and commit+push contract.

The projects.json write path (projects_store.set_project/remove_project -> _write_record) lacks the shared write_lock, atomic commit, and auto-push semantics required by the store invariant, enabling unauthorized hand-commits to corrupt live branch state.

Restoration of origin/tickets:.bridge_state/projects.json to the canonical single-project seed state {version:1, legacy_default:REB, projects:{}} resolves the outage; empty projects map causes the fan-out to fall back to the single configured project REB.

Seven hardening tickets (A–G) including fetcher resilience, bridge-state write-lock adoption, project visibility preflight validation, and syntactic write-time project-key validation prevent future recurrence.
